questions: Are you fully awake and aware of what is happening during these movements?
Can you remember everything that happens during each episode?
Can you stop the movements briefly if you deliberately try?
Do the movements come in separate episodes with normal periods between them?
Have you ever completely lost consciousness during an episode?
Have you bitten your tongue or lost control of your urine during an episode?
Did the movements begin after starting or increasing a medication?
Have you recently taken metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol, or another medicine for nausea or agitation?
Have you used alcohol, cocaine, amphetamines, or another recreational drug recently?
Do you have severe headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?
Do you have new weakness, numbness, facial drooping, or difficulty speaking?
Do you feel an irresistible urge to move before the movements begin?
Have you had similar movements or seizures in the past?
Have you recently had vomiting, diarrhea, poor food intake, or heavy sweating?
orders: Continuous video-EEG monitoring during an episode
Bedside neurologic examination with testing for distractibility, entrainment, and variability of the movements
Serum electrolytes including calcium, magnesium, sodium, potassium, phosphate, bicarbonate, and renal function
Complete blood count, liver function tests, and inflammatory markers
Urine toxicology screen and serum ethanol level
Electroencephalogram after the episode or movement-free period
Serum creatine kinase and urinalysis for myoglobin
Lumbar puncture with cerebrospinal-fluid analysis, only if encephalopathy or other signs of central nervous system infection or inflammation are found
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
distribution of the movements (one side, both, face, limbs)
effect of voluntary action and anxiety
